'''James M. Schlatter''' (27 July 1930 – 15 November 2019) was an American chemist. He is known for discovering [[aspartame]].

== Biography ==
James M. Schlatter was born on 27 July 1930 in [[Brazil, Indiana]] to Howard Schlatter and Bertha Schwab.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2019-11-17 |title=James M. Schlatter |url=https://www.suncommercial.com/banner_graphic/archives/article_8be16985-3e19-503a-982d-97afbd6c07b5.html |access-date=2026-03-12 |website=Vincennes Sun-Commercial |language=en}}</ref>

As a child, he attended the Brazil Lutheran Church. He graduated Brazil Senior High School in 1948 and [[DePauw University]] in 1952. In 1954, he obtained a master's degree in chemistry at Indiana University.<ref name=":0" />

He served in the [[United States Army|U.S Army]]. He worked as a chemist for [[G. D. Searle & Company]].<ref name=":0" />

In December 1965,<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last=Stegink |first=Lewis D. |title=Aspartame : Physiology and Biochemistry |last2=Filer Jr. |first2=L.J |publisher=Marcel Dekker, Inc. |year=1984 |isbn=0-8247-7206-7 |location=New York |language=en|pages=4}}</ref> Schlatter unintentionally discovered [[aspartame]] while working on an anti-ulcer drug. [[Aspartic acid]] and [[phenylalanine]] had been [[Chemical synthesis|synthesized]]<ref>Nill, Ashley G. (2000). "[https://dash.harvard.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/7312037c-a98d-6bd4-e053-0100007fdf3b/content The History of Aspartame]", p. 8.</ref> by Dr. Mazur, and Schlatter then heated the result in a flask with [[methanol]]. The mixture bumped onto the outside of the flask, and then got on Schlatter's fingers. When he later licked his finger to pick up a piece of paper, he "noticed a very strong, sweet taste". He took a little bit of the crystallized aspartyl-phenylalanine methyl ester (aspartame) and tasted it, and found that it was the same substance he had earlier tasted.<ref name=":1" />

Schlatter died on 15 November 2019 at his residence in [[Avon, Indiana]].<ref name=":0" />
